newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - ICI sells bulk chemicals to DuPont.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - ICI sells bulk chemicals to DuPont.

text.p: Imperial Chemical Industries Plc said on Monday it was selling most of its bulk chemicals businesses to DuPont Co for $3.0 billion in a swift further move in the transformation of the company.
ICI is was selling its polyester polymer businesses, its titanium dioxide operations outside North America and polyester film businesses to DuPont.
The sale comes hard on the heels of completion of ICI's purchase of speciality chemicals businesses from Unilever Plc/NV and the public offering last week of its stake in ICI Australia.
The market greeted Monday's news, with ICI shares quoted up 40 pence, or 4.7 percent, at 850-1/2 before the official opening.
"The deal looks very good and the shares should be looking better...especially the speed of the deal will be taken well by the market," one share dealer said.
ICI chief executive Charles Miller Smith said, "I am delighted that we have been able to move so quickly to establish the new basic shape of the group."
The DuPont sale virtually completes within three months the group's three-year divestment target of three billion pounds against the 4.9 billion pounds cost of acquiring the Unilever businesses.

The deal will enhance earnings in 1998 and confirmed a decisive strategic shift in the ICI portfolio away from heavy bulk chemicals, the company said in a statement. It would also significantly reduce ICI's borrowings.
ICI also said on Monday it expected that group profits before tax and exceptionals would be 160 million pounds in the six months to June 30, down from 367 million last year.
It said the fall was as expected, with strong sales, but pricing -- particularly in polyester and tioxide -- as well as the strong pound restrained profitability.

"After the recent acquisition of the former Unilever Speciality Chemicals businesses, this series of disposals confirms the decisive shift in ICI's portfolio," Miller Smith said pf the DuPont deal. "The transactions represent real value for ICI and its shareholders."
"This is another major milestone in creating a new ICI for the new century, Miller Smith added.
The businesses to be sold to DuPont contributed aggregate sales of 1.45 billion pounds and a trading profit of 17 million in 1996. At end-1996 they had aggregate net assets of 1.12 billion pounds.
The businesses sold to DuPont are as follows:
Polyester polymer and intermediates for a consideration of $1.6 billion
Titanium dioxide (excluding north America) for a consideration of $750 million.
Polyester film for $650 million

ICI said it was developing options for the disposal of its North American titanium dioxide businesses. DuPont has agreed that if the proceeds to ICI from the sale of these are less than $150 million, DuPont will cover any deficit.
ICI said it has anticipated the disposals will create a small profit over book value before the write-off of purchased goodwill in tioxide of 130 million pounds.
